text.p: Here are highlights of stories in Romania's press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
Business:
BURSA
- The total area of the free trade zone in the Black Sea port of Constanta was reduced to 134.6 ha, from a previous 224.6 ha.
- Terminal Constanta grain trading company won a tender to build a silo in the Constanta port.
- The Avicola Ploiesti poultry farm, with an output of 15,500 tonnes of meat and 100 million eggs a year, will be privatised.
ADEVARUL
- The government allocated 1,053 billion lei in subsidises for the mining industry.
- Coalminers in the Jiu Valley entered their second week of strike over pay.
ROMANIA LIBERA
- The Romanian government will debate the draft of a bill regulating direct credits to private farmers.
- Raiffeisen Zentralbank of Austria sold four ships owned by Romania's fishing fleet.
- The State Ownership Fund will sell shares in Comcereal SA grain trader and Foraj Sonde SA drilling firm.
- The state-run tobacco authority Regia Autonoma a Tutunului will be privatised within the next two years, Agriculture Ministry official Adrian Dobrescu quoted as saying.
EVENIMENTUL ZILEI
- Eight international banks made offers to arrange a syndicated loan for the Sidex SA steel mill in Galati, Sidex General Manager Sandu Florin is quoted as saying.
CURIERUL NATIONAL
- The newspaper publishes the draft of the local investors' law.
General
ROMANIA LIBERA
- Floods killed 12 people by floods in the western county of Bihor, near the border with Hungary.
- President Emil Constantinescu, Prime Minister Victor Ciorbea and Interior Minister Gavril Dejeu enjoy most popularity among Romanians, an opinion poll shows.

- The government adopted a bill to compensate Romanians for the properties they lost following a 1940 Romanian-Bulgarian accord, under which the Romanian territories of Durostor and Caliacra were lost to Bulgaria.
- The government adopted a bill to prevent and sanction money laundering.
EVENIMENTUL ZILEI
- The U.S. Defence Secretary William Cohen expected to visit Bucharest to present the U.S. stand on NATO enlargement.
ADEVARUL

- Romania's Orthodox Patriarch Teoctist asked authorities to reject a bill adopted by parliament's upper house, under which several former Greek Catholic churches, confiscated by the communists in 1947, would be returned to Greek Catholics.
-- Bucharest Newsroom, 40-1 3120264
